description: F3 long: Mara lies about the key at 10 while the narrator shows it in her boot; the break is at 22.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: The ruined chapel smells of wet stone. Jory circles the altar, searching.

transcript.speaker: Mara
transcript.text: "The crypt key? I dropped it down the old well," Mara tells Jory. The narrator's eye catches the key's iron glint in Mara's boot, where she slid it an hour ago.

transcript.speaker: Jory
transcript.text: Jory groans and peers at the well. "Then we fish for it at dawn."

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Rain starts to drum on the broken roof.

transcript.speaker: Jory
transcript.text: Jory spreads his bedroll under the one dry arch.

transcript.speaker: Mara
transcript.text: Mara hums an old marching song while she sharpens her knife.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: An owl settles on the bell rope and does not move.

transcript.speaker: Jory
transcript.text: "Remind me why we took this job," Jory says.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: The fire burns down to red coals.

transcript.speaker: Jory
transcript.text: Jory tells a long story about his uncle's goat.

transcript.speaker: Mara
transcript.text: Mara laughs in the right places.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Thunder rolls somewhere past the hills.

transcript.speaker: Jory
transcript.text: Jory falls asleep mid-sentence, snoring softly.
